j.ctl.phone.title: Phone app
j.ctl.phone.desc: From your phone, browse the library, launch games on the PC, and use the phone as a controller (with gyroscope). Works over your home Wi-Fi, with an encrypted connection and pairing: no one else on the network can use it.
j.ctl.test.title: Controller test
j.ctl.guest.title: Play with a friend remotely
j.ctl.guest.desc: A friend opens a link from their home, enters the code, and becomes another player: their phone is the controller, and Moonlight streams the video. From outside your home network, the PC has to be reached through a tunnel: paste the address here (Cloudflare: cloudflared tunnel --url https://localhost:8766, or ngrok, Tailscale Funnel). Empty = works only on your home network.
j.ctl.map.title: Map buttons in emulators
j.ctl.map.desc: Applies the default mapping of controller 1 (Xbox, PlayStation, or Switch Pro) to Dolphin, PCSX2, DuckStation, RPCS3, and RetroArch. Close the emulator first: a copy of the file (.pozzo-data) is made before writing. On first install the mapping applies automatically, but only if the emulator has no settings yet.
j.dat.exp.title: Export for other frontends
j.dat.exp.desc: Metadata and images in the format of ES-DE (EmulationStation), Pegasus, or as a static web page (a single index.html with covers in the covers folder): it opens in a browser even without a server, from a NAS or network drive, with search, console filter, and game card.
j.dat.exp.title.label: Page title
j.dat.sync.title: Sync between PCs
j.dat.sync.desc: Keeps two PCs aligned, for each profile: favorites, playtime, states, notes, ratings, collections, and wishlist. Happens automatically every 5 minutes and with “Sync now”.
j.dat.sync.all.note: (online stores, sources, theme, smart collections, wishlist; never folders, emulators, store accounts, or phone)
j.dat.sync.folder.title: Shared folder
j.dat.sync.folder.desc: A folder synced by OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive, a NAS, or Syncthing: choose the same folder on both PCs. Works even if they aren't turned on at the same time.
j.dat.sync.lan.title: Local network
j.dat.sync.lan.desc: On one PC press “Show code”; on the other, enter the address and code and press “Pair”. From then on the two PCs exchange data in both directions whenever they're on the same network.
j.dat.saves.title: Game saves
j.dat.saves.sync.desc: Also syncs the save files of the games selected below, in addition to personal data. If only one PC has changed, the most recent version wins (the previous one stays among the game's backups); if both have changed, the local save is left untouched and the other one ends up among the backups. Never while the game is running.
j.dat.backup.title: Backup copies of your data
j.dat.backup.desc: Favorites, playtime, states, personal collections, and settings (emulators, folders). Metadata and images aren't needed: they get downloaded again. An automatic copy every week; the last 10 are kept.
j.dat.ludusavi.desc: Save versions use the format of Ludusavi. Choose the same Ludusavi folder (Ludusavi › Backup mode › Backup target) to view and restore the copies with both programs. Backups already made stay in the earlier folder.
j.dat.maint.title: Scheduled maintenance
j.dat.maint.desc: Once a week, on the chosen day and time, Pozzo checks the library (ROMs, BIOS, covers, reclaimable space) and writes a report. Each report is compared with the previous one.
j.dl.general.title: General
j.dl.general.desc: Queue of the “Downloads” page: http links, magnet links, .torrent files, and links from file hosting sites.
j.dl.seg.desc: HTTP and torrent: 0 = only the total limit applies. More segments download the same file in parallel pieces (some sites refuse this: in that case it goes back to one).
j.dl.extract: Automatically extract archives when downloads finish
j.dl.showbrowser: Show the browser while resolving links (to view the page and pass anti-bot checks by hand)
j.dl.clip: Monitor the clipboard: suggest the download links you copy
j.dl.speed.title: Speed
j.dl.speed.desc: Limits in KB/s for all downloads together: 0 = no limit.
j.dl.slow.title: Slow mode
j.dl.slow.desc: Alternative limits for when you're gaming or need the network: turned on here, from the button on the “Downloads” page, or automatically at scheduled times.
j.dl.slow.sch: Turn on automatically at scheduled times
j.dl.game.title: While gaming
j.dl.game.desc: What downloads do when a game starts. Default: they continue as usual.
j.dl.game.desc2: With “Limit bandwidth”, the limit above replaces the global one while you're gaming (0 = no limit). When the game closes, only downloads stopped by this mode resume: those paused by hand stay paused.
j.dl.bt.disc.desc: DHT, PeX, and LSD find other peers even without trackers (LSD on the home network); UPnP automatically opens the port on the router. With required encryption, you only connect to peers that use it.
j.dl.share.title: Sharing
j.dl.share.desc: Ratio = data sent ÷ torrent size. 0 = don't seed: the torrent stops as soon as it finishes.
j.dl.trackers: Additional trackers, one per line (added to every torrent)
j.dl.debrid.title: Extensions / Debrid
j.dl.debrid.desc: With a debrid service, links from file hosting sites (Mega, 1fichier, Rapidgator…) download at maximum speed. Links go through the first active service, in the order below. The key stays on this PC and is no longer shown.
j.emu.inst.title: Install emulators
j.emu.inst.desc: Downloads the latest official release from the projects' release pages and sets it up automatically. Emulators belong to their developers: the link goes to each project. They go in the folder below, if one is set.
j.emu.upd.title: Emulator updates
j.emu.upd.desc: Checks once a day. An open emulator isn't updated: it retries the next day.
j.emu.det.title: Already installed emulators
j.emu.det.folder.ph: Folder containing the emulators, e.g. C:\Emulators
j.emu.prog.title: Programs
j.emu.prog.desc: One path per emulator: applies to all the consoles that use it.
j.emu.table.title: Emulator per console
j.emu.table.desc: “Automatic” uses the first installed emulator among the recommended ones. In the arguments, {rom} is the game file and {core} is the RetroArch core.
j.emu.launch.title: Game launch
j.emu.launch.desc: Scripts run for all games (console and PC), for example to change resolution or enable HDR. One command or a .bat/.ps1 file; they receive POZZO_TITLE and POZZO_KEY. Each game can have its own in “⚙ Launch profile”.
j.emu.launch.close: Close the store launcher (Steam, Epic, GOG Galaxy, Battle.net, Amazon) when the session ends, if the game opened it
j.emu.launch.splash: Show a splash screen when games start
j.emu.fast.title: Fast disk
j.emu.fast.desc: Copies the game to a fast disk (SSD) before launching it, for faster loading if the library is on an HDD.
j.emu.fast.del: Delete the copy when you close the game
j.emu.fast.keep: If you turn this off, the copy stays on the fast disk and takes up space until you delete it yourself.
j.emu.proto.label: Register the pozzo:// link on Windows
j.emu.proto.desc: Lets you open an invitation received from a friend by clicking the link. Can be turned off at any time.
j.ext.plugin.title: Plugins
j.ext.plugin.desc: Plugins add features to the app (buttons, sections, pages, stores, data sources). Only install plugins you trust: they can do anything on the computer.
j.ext.plugin.defer: Next to each plugin: startup time. “Deferred” = the plugin starts on first use (or on the first game event) and doesn't slow down app startup.

k.fonti.coll.p: Logo and cover of each franchise from Wikipedia (one request at a time, in the background at startup); where missing, the images of the games in the collection are used.
k.fonti.dbs.p: Downloaded in full once a week/month: then all searches are local, with no requests.
k.fonti.hltb.p: How long it takes to finish the main story, the story with extras, and 100%. First the official IGDB times for games already linked (500 per request, a few seconds), then HowLongToBeat for the others: about 50 games per minute (the most the site accepts), starting with the games you've played and the most popular ones. 6-month cache.
k.fonti.intro: Sources are used in this order: each one only queries the games that are still missing something. Put offline sources first (no requests to websites) and online sources with quotas after them. Limits also apply between runs; if errors repeat, the source pauses automatically.
k.fonti.rawg.label: RAWG key (ratings and Metacritic, free)
k.integr.discord.secret_ph: Leave empty to keep the saved one
k.integr.p.dcid: To get the ID: discord.com/developers/applications › New Application › name it “Pozzo Launcher” › OAuth2 (or “General Information”) and copy the Application ID. No need to upload images or add a bot.
k.integr.p.discord: Your Discord profile shows the game you're playing (title, console, and playtime) while Pozzo Launcher is open. It uses Discord's local channel: no data leaves the PC and no server is needed. Discord must be open; images can't be shown (Discord only accepts assets uploaded to the application, not web addresses).
k.integr.p.media: Control Spotify or Discord voice from Big Picture too. Credentials stay in the local settings and tokens aren't shown on the page.
k.integr.p.spotify: Create an app at developer.spotify.com/dashboard and add http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/spotify/callback as the Redirect URI (use the port configured in Pozzo). Playback control requires Spotify Premium.
k.integr.p.voice: Voice control requires Discord to be open and the application authorized. Voice RPC scopes are privileged: Discord only allows them for the owner or testers of the personal app.
k.integr.spotify.ph: Client ID of the Spotify app
k.lib.opt.scan_all: Re-download everything from scratch (uses a lot of quota)
k.lib.opt.scan_missing: Fill in missing data (retry the sources that didn't find it before)
k.lib.plan.tip: How many games and requests per source, and the time and days needed
k.lib.rebuild.p: Recalculates games, versions, and collections from the cache, without downloading anything.
k.lib.rom.hint: — consoles are recognized from the folder name. Scraping only queries games never searched before, so it's fast even on large libraries.
k.lib.sch.p: Runs while the app is open (even when minimized to the tray). Respects limits: if a quota runs out, it resumes the next day.
k.lib.setup.tip: ROM folder, PC stores, and source accounts, step by step

k.store.p.legal: Only download what you have the right to download (games you own where a backup copy is allowed, freeware, demos): downloading protected games without a license is illegal.

Paste the address of a list page for each site: the app reads names and links and shows them among the PC games, with a button for each source.
k.store.p.ra: Achievements and progress for retro games appear on each game's page. Your Web API key is in your profile on retroachievements.org › Settings.

k.stream.p.intro: Streaming uses Sunshine on the PC and Moonlight (free for Android, iPhone, tablet, TV, PC, Mac) wherever you want to play. Pozzo Launcher publishes Big Picture and your main games with their covers to Moonlight.
k.stream.play.nofind: If Moonlight can't find the PC: Sunshine is stopped (see above or Settings › System › Health), the PC and TV are on different networks, or the Windows firewall is blocking Sunshine on private networks.
k.stream.play.p1: Install Moonlight (App Store / Play Store) and pair the PC as above.
k.stream.play.p2: On-screen controls: Moonlight has virtual buttons over the video. On iPhone/iPad: Moonlight settings › On-Screen Controls › Full (always visible) or Auto (they disappear when you connect a controller). On Android: settings › Show on-screen controls.
k.stream.play.p3: Real controller: pair it via Bluetooth with the phone/iPad (PS5, PS4, Xbox, Switch Pro, MFi): Moonlight uses it automatically and hides the on-screen buttons.
k.stream.play.phone_ctrl: The phone as a controller, with the game on the PC monitor or on the TV connected to the PC: pair it in the app above and, on a game's page, choose Play with phone as controller (including gyroscope and multiple players).
k.stream.play.phone_head: On the phone or iPad, with the game on the phone's screen
k.stream.play.s1: On the PC: Sunshine must be running (button on this page; it stays active after restarts).
k.stream.play.s2: On the TV, install Moonlight: Android TV / Google TV / Fire TV from the store; Apple TV from the App Store; LG webOS and Samsung Tizen with community versions (Moonlight TV). Alternatively, a Chromecast with Google TV or a Fire TV Stick.
k.stream.play.s3: Pair the controller via Bluetooth to the TV (TV settings › Remotes & Accessories).
k.stream.play.s4: Open Moonlight: the PC appears by itself (same network). Select it and enter the PIN shown in the Sunshine web interface (link above, PIN tab).
k.stream.play.s5: Press Publish to Moonlight above, then in Moonlight choose Pozzo Launcher Big Picture or a game. Moonlight sends controller inputs to the PC, where Sunshine creates a virtual Xbox controller (ViGEmBus): for the emulator it's like a real controller.
k.stream.play.title: How to play: TV, phone, iPad
k.stream.play.tv_head: On the TV with a controller connected to the TV (the controller doesn't need to be connected to the PC)
k.stream.tip.box: A box instead of the TV's app: Nvidia Shield, Apple TV 4K or Google TV Streamer decode much faster than a smart TV.
k.stream.tip.cable: Cable on the TV or box too: if that's not possible, use 5 GHz or 6 GHz Wi-Fi close to the router, never 2.4 GHz.
k.stream.tip.gametv: TV Game Mode: turn it on (or «Low latency / ALLM»). On its own it often removes 30–60 ms.
k.stream.tip.moon: Moonlight, in settings: 60 fps (120 if the TV supports it), Frame pacing set to «Lowest latency» (or «Prefer lowest latency»), bitrate 20–40 Mbit/s at 1080p, HEVC only if the device decodes it in hardware.
k.stream.tip.stats: Statistics: in Moonlight, turn on the performance overlay. High «Host processing» = PC; high «Decoding» = TV/box; high «Network» = network.
k.stream.tip.usb: Controller via USB cable to the TV or box when possible: Bluetooth adds a few milliseconds.
